note_en: L1(i): Apache-2.0 (LICENSE file only on GitHub). D1(i): Nemotron and FineWeb2 sources listed, plus an undisclosed proprietary Korean crawl of ~1.37T tokens ("not an exhaustive inventory"). Sovereign AI program: selected.
MIT. D1: "45T tokens… re-bootstrapped it from Common Crawl" (no source list). R1: PDF report in the repository. R2(i): one benchmark reproduction via API.
Apache-2.0; ERNIEKit pre-training code (Apache-2.0). P2: Base model only. R2(i): generic evaluation tool, no reproduction kit.
MIT. R1(i): cites the GLM-5 report, but starts from a new, unpublished base.

L1: revocable license; mandatory acceptable-use policy; branding; new license required above 10M MAU or for competitors. Uses the Qwen2.5-VL vision encoder. Eliminated from the Korean sovereign AI program for failing the independence criterion (MSIT, Jan. 2026).
L1: Apache-2.0 tag without a LICENSE file, plus an acceptable-use policy declared binding ("you agree to be bound") on weights and derivatives.

L1(i): Apache-2.0; the model card states that users "are not allowed to engage in any malicious activities… violating LG AI's ethical principles", a substantive restriction that is neither incorporated into the license nor tied to an acceptance mechanism (binding test, Table S7); N under the strict reading. Upcycled from K-EXAONE (LG). D1: "8T tokens" and categories only. Sovereign AI program: selected.
L1: model-as-a-service above US$20M requires a "separate agreement"; branding above 100M MAU. Epoch AI labels it "non-commercial", which the license text does not support.
L1(i): MIT declared only in README/metadata. D3(i): data summary in the EU template. C1(i): Megatron patch and demo, without the 1T training recipe.

L1: Llama 4 Community License (separate license above 700M monthly active users; "Built with Llama") plus acceptable-use policy that excludes EU-domiciled persons from the multimodal models. L2: manual approval. D1 includes public Instagram and Facebook posts; no source list.
MIT. D1: size only ("more than 35 trillion tokens"). C3(i): supported only in SGLang. No technical report.
L1(i): MIT declared only in metadata. D1: "27T tokens". R1(i): only the architecture paper of V2-Flash.
L1: grant "for non-commercial purposes" while another section regulates commercial use; US$20M threshold; branding; military use prohibited. R1(i): only a paper on attention.

MIT. D1(i): ~70% of data listed (Nemotron), the rest proprietary. C1(i): MIT training framework with example configurations only. P2(i): Motif-3-Beta and Base. Sovereign AI program: added in 2026, dropped in the second stage.

L1(i): OpenMDW-1.1 ("without restriction"), an open license for model materials, not an OSI-approved software license. D1(i)/D2(i): data largely published, partly behind manual approval; a few entries "Undisclosed"; long-context data not released. P2(i): Base only.
Dolma 3 (ODC-By) with reconstruction tooling; OLMo-core, open-instruct and OLMES (Apache-2.0); intermediate checkpoints published.
L1: "Qwen3.8-Max" license with thresholds (100M MAU or US$20M per month; MaaS above US$50M). Qwen3.8-Max itself is API-only.

L1(i): modified Apache-2.0 (derivative names must begin with "Solar"; "Built with Solar"); custom license, not OSI-approved. Partly derived from Solar Open 1 (Upstage). Sovereign AI program: selected.
Apache-2.0. No information on data. Fine-tuning code only.

L1(i): card states "mit", but use is "subject to the Model License", which could not be found. D1(i): 22 public datasets with links, plus summarily described NIA data. Sovereign AI program: eliminated in the first stage.

L1: Apache-2.0; the usage policy is binding ("By using… you agree") but only requires compliance with applicable law (binding test, Table S7). D1: "trillions of tokens, with a focus on STEM, coding, and general knowledge" (no source list). R2: evaluation code in gpt_oss/evals (AIME, GPQA, HealthBench); corrected after second coding.

Derived from EuroLLM-9B (EU). L1(i): Apache-2.0 only in the Hugging Face tag (GitHub declares none). D2(i): Arquivo.pt reconstructable via arquivo_processing (no LICENSE). C2(i): datatrove-amalia is Apache-2.0, but arquivo_processing has no license. P2(i): stage checkpoints only.
(i) No repository or public weights; API access according to the press. No primary source available.

Continued pre-training of TinyLlama 1.1B (Singapore). L1: no license declared (model and dataset). D1(i): "150B Portuguese tokens from the ClassiCC-PT corpus". P2: 50B and 100B checkpoints. R1: "Coming soon".
Derived from Gemma 3 4B (United States). L1: Gemma Terms of Use (prohibited-use policy). D1: "~13 billion tokens… Scientific Articles… Wikipedia", no source list.
Derived from Llama 3.1 8B Instruct (base_model metadata). L1(i): declares MIT, but the Llama 3.1 license applies to derivatives. R1(i): paper on an earlier version.
Derived from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (China). L1: Apache-2.0 plus mandatory acceptance of "Acceptable Use Guidelines" (MOF §4.3). L2: access form. D1: "synthetically generated dataset…", no sources.

Derived from Llama 3.1 70B (United States). L1: Llama 3.1 Community License. D1: source list deferred to a "data catalog". D2(i): partially open corpus, behind a form, restricted for large firms. C2: repositories without LICENSE. R2(i): benchmarks and harness fork, without integrated tasks.

CC BY 4.0 (open permissive license). Source table (GigaVerbo, Ulysses Tesemõ, Portuguese Wikipedia); corpus pipeline, tokenizer, Megatron pre-training and benchmarks on GitHub. R1: arXiv 2608.30114. P2: not found.
API only. R1: arXiv 2603.10213. D1: "large-scale Portuguese corpus combined with a Brazilian legal corpus", no sources.
Derived from LLaMA-1-7B (United States). L1: LLaMA-1 license, "research purposes only". D1(i): single source (ClueWeb22) and filters described.

State-backed (SoberanIA, Piauí). No model card, no license, manual approval; base not declared (GGUF metadata: qwen3 architecture, ~32.8B parameters). D2/D3: no datasets or data card published (corrected from ND to N after second coding). The Jabuticaba corpus (CC BY-SA, manual approval) is not linked to the model in any document.
Native pre-training on Portuguese and English; GigaVerbo-v2 and llm-foundry (Apache-2.0); checkpoints every 5,000 steps.
Derived from Qwen3-4B-Base (China). Own stage fully open; inherits the undisclosed data and code of Qwen3-4B-Base.

L1: Apache-2.0 plus a binding usage policy requiring indemnification of ETH/EPFL and data-protection compliance, without restricting purposes (binding test, Table S7). D2 via reconstruction scripts (pretrain-data, Apache-2.0). D3(i): data documented in the paper (Sec. 3), no separate data card. C1: Megatron-LM fork (BSD-3) tagged for Apertus 1; the unlicensed pretrain-code repository belongs to Apertus 1.5.

L1: BigScience RAIL v1.0 with 13 use restrictions (including medical advice and administration of justice). D2(i): ROOTS behind an automatic form (Ethical Charter). C1(i): repositories under OSI licenses, but RAIL extends to "Complementary Material". R2(i): results and harness published; the card warns some results "were not correct".
D2(i): pre-tokenized data published; the original Pile mirror was offline on Oct. 23, 2026; the Pile contains copyrighted sources.
Apache-2.0. D1(i): public mixture described. D2(i): mid-training and post-training data "will be uploaded later". D3(i): data summary in the EU template. R1: blog only.
MIT for R1 code and weights (V3 has its own Model License). Built on DeepSeek-V3-Base. D1: "14.8T… tokens", no sources. R2: "internal evaluation framework".
Representative row: API only. R1 not assessed (system cards exist, without data descriptions).

L1: acceptable-use policy, 700M MAU threshold, "Llama" name prefix for derivatives. D1: "~15 trillion tokens… publicly available sources" and proportions, no sources. R2: evaluation details behind a form, no code.
Apache-2.0. No technical report (blog only). R2(i): MM-MT-Bench published; mistral-evals has no LICENSE.
Apache-2.0 (metadata; LICENSE file not found). No information on data; arXiv 2401.04088 covers only Mixtral 8x7B.

Distilled from the proprietary Muse Spark. L1(i): Apache-2.0; USAGE_POLICY.md lists prohibited uses ("You should not use") but is neither incorporated into the license nor tied to an acceptance mechanism (binding test, Table S7); N under the strict reading. R2(i): evaluation data and methodology, without code.

Work in progress. D1(i)/D3(i): token table per source in a README of an unlicensed repository. D2: mixture in internal paths. C2(i): training-data-packer is Apache-2.0, but decontamination code is unlicensed. R1: no report.
